Include exactly 13 numbers in the response. In the context of a hypothetical, write the jacket blurb for a thriller where a modern day operative of the FBI, ends up back in the early 1960's having to use her knowledge of "future" forensics to leave clues to enable her modern colleagues to catch a time-hopping serial-killer, before he dies.assistant
response:
"When FBI operative Rachel Jenkins is sent back in time to the early 1960s, she finds herself in the midst of a decades-old mystery. A serial killer, known only as 'The Timekeeper,' has been terrorizing the nation, leaving a trail of bodies in his wake. But this is no ordinary killer - he's a time-hopper, able to move through the ages with ease.

As Rachel navigates the unfamiliar streets of 1960s America, she must use her knowledge of future forensics to leave clues that will aid her modern colleagues in catching The Timekeeper. But with each passing day, she realizes that she's not the only one who knows the killer's true identity.

With the help of a local detective, Jack, Rachel must unravel the threads of a decades-old conspiracy that goes all the way to the top. As they dig deeper, they uncover a web of deceit and corruption that threatens to destroy everything they hold dear.

But time is running out - The Timekeeper is getting closer to his next victim, and Rachel knows that she must act fast if she wants to prevent another murder. With the clock ticking down, Rachel must use all her skills and knowledge to outsmart the killer and bring him to justice.

As the stakes grow higher, Rachel finds herself in a desperate game of cat and mouse, with the fate of the world hanging in the balance. Can she use her knowledge of the future to catch The Timekeeper, or will he always be one step ahead?

13 clues, 6 decades, 1 killer - the clock is ticking. Will Rachel be able to solve the mystery before it's too late?"
